story.head: The Panthers played last night
paras: The Bruins have won three straight, the last a 6-2 rout of Pittsburgh. The Panthers (9-5-2) beat Chicago 5-3 on Wednesday. The Panthers played last night, and the Bruins are rested. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Panthers fifth (tied for 11th in the NHL) and the Bruins first (tied for third). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.
The Panthers’ record (.625) is about what their chances are worth. The Bruins’ record (.735) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.562), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Panthers are the league’s most physical team (1st) and kill penalties well (1st). They also forecheck harder than anyone (1st), so the Cats hound the puck, but the Bruins sit back. The Bruins have had the league’s best goaltending (1st) and leave the shooting to their forwards (2nd lowest), but rarely threaten on the penalty kill (31st). Boston has allowed 2.35 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. Put that together and expect a chippy, heavy game.

Matthew Tkachuk (4 G / 18 A / 22 P in 16 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Sam Reinhart (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 16 GP) has a team-high nine goals, with eight points in his last five games and seven goals in ten games against Boston since 2023-24. The Bruins’ scoring runs through David Pastrňák (8 G / 14 A / 22 P in 17 GP), who has a point in five straight games against Florida.
Akira Schmid (5-2-1 / .888 SV% in 7 GS) is in line to start for Florida. Jeremy Swayman (8-3-1 / .912 SV% in 12 GS) has been a rock in net for Boston and will likely start.
At home, Marco Sturm likes to send Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Hagens out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against B. Tkachuk, Bennett and M. Tkachuk.
